lines: Rotates an X/Y point in three dimensions and puts out the rotated X, Y and Z coordinates
Rotates the point around the X axis, from no rotation at the left to a full turn at the right
Rotates the point around the Y axis, from no rotation at the left to a full turn at the right
Rotates the point around the Z axis, from no rotation at the left to a full turn at the right
Adds to the rotation around the X axis, a full turn per 10V
Adds to the rotation around the Y axis, a full turn per 10V
Adds to the rotation around the Z axis, a full turn per 10V
The X coordinate of the point to rotate, read as -5V to 5V
The Y coordinate of the point to rotate, read as -5V to 5V
The X coordinate after rotation, -5V to 5V
The Y coordinate after rotation, -5V to 5V
The Z coordinate after rotation, -5V to 5V; the incoming point is taken as flat, so any depth here is made by the rotation
Note — with nothing patched into the X and Y inputs the point is at the origin, so all three outputs stay at 0V whatever the knobs are set to
Puts out a trigger or a gate when the voltage at CV IN matches a chosen note
Picks the note to match, through the twelve semitones from C to B
Picks the octave to match, from -1 to 8, with C4 at 0V; turned fully counter-clockwise it reads All, and the note matches in every octave
The voltage tested against the chosen note; with nothing patched here the output stays at 0V
In the clocked output modes, only a rising edge here can produce a trigger or gate
Carries 10V when the incoming voltage matches the chosen note, as a trigger or a gate
Menu — Output Mode — Trigger, Gate, Clocked Trigger or Clocked Gate
Menu — Trigger Length — how long the trigger pulse lasts, from 1ms to 200ms
Menu — Tolerance Level — how far the incoming voltage may stray from the note and be taken as a match, from Exact (0) to Very Coarse (0.5)
Menu — Notation — Sharp or Flat, setting how the readout names a black note
Bouncing-ball sequencer: eight columns, each with a ball that travels up and down its column one row per clock and fires a trigger at the end of its travel
A rising edge moves every ball one row; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge returns every ball to the bottom of its column
A 10ms 10V trigger from that column, fired as its ball turns around
Note — drag in the grid to set how tall each column is, which sets how many clocks that column's ball takes to come back round
Note — every column starts one row tall, and a column one row tall fires nothing, so no trigger is put out until the grid is drawn
Menu — Column Settings — All Columns and Column #1 through Column #8, each holding that column's Trigger Location
Menu — Trigger Location — Bottom, Top or Both, choosing which end of the column fires that column's trigger; reached through Column Settings
Plays one loaded WAV file over and over, with a volume slider and a stereo pair of outputs
Sets the playback level, from silence to the full level of the file
A rising edge restarts the file from its beginning
The left channel of the file; a mono file is carried on both outputs
The right channel of the file; a mono file is carried on both outputs
Note — the outputs stay silent until a WAV file is loaded: right-click the panel and click the item under the Sample label, which reads [ EMPTY ] until then
Note — the waveform of the loaded file is drawn across the panel, and the file plays over and over on its own with no trigger patched
Menu — Output Range — rescales the audio into one of eight voltage ranges, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with -5.0 to 5.0 to start with
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Sample — the item under this label loads the WAV file, and prints the filename it holds
Plays sixteen loaded WAV files, each fired by one channel of a polyphonic trigger input, and mixes them to one stereo pair
A polyphonic trigger input, one channel per sample: a rising edge on channel 1 plays the first sample, channel 2 the second, and so on through all sixteen
The left channel of all sixteen players added together
The right channel of all sixteen players added together
Note — nothing plays until WAV files are loaded from the right-click menu, either one at a time or sixteen at once from a folder
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Load individual samples — the sixteen numbered items under this label each open a file browser for that sample slot, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Load first 16 WAV files from a folder — opens a folder browser and puts that folder's first sixteen WAV files into the sixteen slots in name order
sampler16p.notes: The module has no panel parameters at all: level, pan and sample choice are fixed, and every sample is fired through the one polyphonic TRIG input.

lines: X/Y pad: drag in the grid to put out a pair of voltages, and the gesture is recorded and played back a step per clock
When on, playback returns to the start of the recorded gesture once the end is reached; when off, playback stops at the end
When on, dragging in the grid overwrites the recording from the playback point onward instead of starting a new one, and playback carries on when the mouse is released
A rising edge moves playback to the next recorded position; with nothing patched here the outputs follow the mouse directly
A rising edge returns playback to the first recorded position
The horizontal position, rising to the right
The vertical position, rising towards the top
Note — pressing in the grid starts a new recording and releasing starts playback of what was drawn
Menu — Output Range — the span of both outputs, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with; honoured only while CLK is unpatched, despite the menu offering it either way
Menu — Tablet Mode — moves the point by hovering over the grid, with no button held
Note — while a clock is patched the outputs run 0-10V whatever the Output Range setting says
xy.notes: Output Range is applied only on the unclocked path; with CLK patched the code writes 0-10V regardless of the menu setting.

lines: Plays one of nine bytebeat equations, an integer expression over a running time counter heard as audio
Picks which of the nine equations is heard
Adds to the equation choice, the nine equations spread over 0-10V
Sets how many samples pass before the time counter advances, from none up to 256, and a longer division lowers the pitch
Adds to the sample division that sets the pitch, its full range over 0-10V
Sets the value of that parameter in the equation, a whole number from 0 to 128
Attenuates the CV for that parameter, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to that parameter after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the full 0 to 128
The audio the equation makes, -5V to 5V
Note — the equation runs on the module's own counter, so the output makes sound with nothing patched in
bytebeat.notes: Inputs 5 and 6 (T and SYNC CLOCK) and output 1 (DEBUG) are declared in the code but have no jack on the panel; the T input is read when connected, the sync clock input is not read at all.

lines: Passes a sixteen-channel polyphonic gate signal through, dropping gates step by step at a probability set per channel and per step
Picks which of the sixteen channels the PERCENTAGE knob edits
Picks which of the sixteen steps the PERCENTAGE knob edits, numbered 1 to 16
Sets the chance that the gate is passed at the chosen channel and step, from 0 to 100 percent; turning either of the other two knobs loads the stored value for the new place
The polyphonic gate signal to be thinned out, one channel per drum part
A rising edge advances the sequence one step, wrapping round after sixteen; clocks arriving within 1ms of a reset are ignored
A rising edge returns the sequence to its first step
The polyphonic gate signal with the dropped gates removed, sixteen channels; a channel that does not pass holds its last voltage until the next step
Note — every channel and every step starts at 100 percent, so gates pass through unchanged until a percentage is lowered
drumrandomizer.notes: The polyphonic gate input and output carry whatever gates are patched in, so neither is given a family beyond that; the code only copies the incoming voltage of channels that pass, so a blocked channel keeps whatever it last carried rather than going to 0V.

lines: Gate sequencer driven by a cellular automaton: a drawn seed pattern runs Conway's rules one generation per clock, and a cell coming to life fires the trigger groups that mark it
Sets how many clocks pass before the pattern is reloaded from the seed, 1 to 64
Selects that trigger group for editing, so clicking in the grid marks which cells fire it; pressing it again returns to play mode
A rising edge runs one generation of the automaton; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge reloads the pattern from the seed and restarts the count
A 10ms 10V trigger, fired whenever a cell marked for that group comes to life in the new generation
Note — the grid is drawn on by dragging across it: with no trigger group selected the drag edits the seed pattern, and with a group selected it marks which cells fire that group
Note — the module comes up with a seed pattern and trigger markings already in place, so it plays as soon as a clock is patched into STEP
CV sequencer that reads its sequences from a text file, one comma-separated line of voltages per sequence
A rising edge advances one step, wrapping to the start at the end of the sequence; clocks arriving within 1ms of a reset are ignored
A rising edge returns the sequence to its first step
Steps back one sequence in the file, wrapping round to the last one
Steps forward one sequence in the file, wrapping round to the first one
Jumps to the first sequence in the file
A rising edge steps back one sequence in the file
A rising edge steps forward one sequence in the file
A rising edge jumps to the first sequence in the file
Shifts which sequence plays without changing the chosen one, -5V to 5V covering twenty sequences either way and wrapping round the file
Attenuates the CV sequence selection, from nothing through to its full range
The voltage written at the current step of the sequence
A 10ms 10V trigger fired as the sequence wraps back to its first step
Note — nothing is put out until a text file is loaded with Load File in the right-click menu; each line of the file is one sequence, read as voltages
Menu — Load File — opens the text file the sequences are read from; the item under it prints the filename, or No file loaded
Gate sequencer that reads its patterns from a text file, one line of ones and zeros per sequence
A rising edge advances one step, wrapping to the start at the end of the sequence; clocks arriving within 1ms of a reset are ignored
A rising edge returns the sequence to its first step
Steps back one sequence in the file, wrapping round to the last one
Steps forward one sequence in the file, wrapping round to the first one
Jumps to the first sequence in the file
A rising edge steps back one sequence in the file
A rising edge steps forward one sequence in the file
A rising edge jumps to the first sequence in the file
Shifts which sequence plays without changing the chosen one, -5V to 5V covering twenty sequences either way and wrapping round the file
Attenuates the CV sequence selection, from nothing through to its full range
A 10ms 10V trigger on every step written as a 1 in the sequence
A 10ms 10V trigger fired as the sequence wraps back to its first step
Note — nothing is put out until a text file is loaded with Load File in the right-click menu; each line of the file is one sequence, read as ones and zeros
Menu — Load File — opens the text file the sequences are read from; the item under it prints the filename, or No file loaded
Sample player holding every WAV file in a chosen folder, with one of them selected by knob or CV
Picks which file in the folder plays, from the first to the last
Attenuates the WAV selection CV, from nothing through to its full range
When on, the file repeats from its start as it reaches its end
A rising edge restarts the chosen file; with nothing patched here the file plays over and over on its own
Adds to the file selection after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the whole folder
Shifts the playback speed by a volt per octave, so 1V plays the file twice as fast and -1V half as fast and backwards below that
The left channel of the file being played
The right channel of the file being played
Nothing in the module writes this output; it stays at 0V, despite the panel printing END
Note — the outputs stay silent until a folder is chosen with Select Directory Containing WAV Files in the right-click menu; the module holds no files of its own
Menu — Trigger Mode — Trigger restarts the file on a rising edge at TRG, Gate plays it only while that input is above 5V
Menu — Select Directory Containing WAV Files — points the module at a folder; its WAV and MP3 files are loaded in name order
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Auto-Increment on Completion — nothing in the module reads this setting in the installed build, so turning it on changes nothing
wavbank.notes: The END output and the Auto-Increment on Completion menu item are wired up in the widget but never written or read in the 2.41.1 processing code, so neither is described here.

lines: Stuttering sample player: a fast clock restarts one of five loaded samples from a chosen position, so the sample skips and repeats
Sets how many clock pulses pass between restarts, none up to ten
Attenuates the DIV CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets where in the sample each restart begins, from its start to its end
Attenuates the POS CV, from nothing through to its full range
Picks which of the five loaded samples plays
Attenuates the WAV selection CV, from nothing through to its full range
Shifts the playback speed by a volt per octave, from -2V to 2V, and below the point where the speed reverses the sample plays backwards
When on, the jump to a new position or a new sample is faded rather than cut, which removes the click
A rising edge advances the stutter count, and a restart happens when the count passes the division; with nothing patched here nothing is restarted
Adds to the restart position after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the whole sample
Adds to the clock division after its attenuator, 0-10V covering none to ten
Adds to the sample selection after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the five samples
Adds to the playback speed, a volt per octave
The sample being played, taken from its left channel
A 10ms 10V trigger each time the sample is restarted
Note — the output stays silent until a WAV file is loaded into at least one of the five slots under Samples in the right-click menu
Menu — Samples — the five numbered items under this label each load a WAV file into that slot, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Retrigger — restarts the sample from its beginning once it has played to its end
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
repeater.notes: Param index 7 is named UNUSED in the source and has no control on the panel.

lines: Breakbeat player: a loaded drum loop is split into sixteen slices and played in an order set by a voltage, in time with an incoming clock
Picks which of the five loaded loops plays
Attenuates the SAMPLE selection CV, from nothing through to its full range
The clock the loop follows, taken at sixteenth notes; the tempo is worked out from the time between two rising edges
A rising edge returns playback to the start of the loop
Picks which of the sixteen slices plays next, 0-10V across the loop; below about 0.6V the playback runs on undisturbed
Adds to the loop selection after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the five loops
A rising edge jumps to the slice chosen by SEQ without waiting for the next clock, which is how a slice is repeated within a beat
Above 5V playback runs backwards through the loop
The left channel of the loop being played
The right channel of the loop being played
Note — the outputs stay silent until a loop is loaded into one of the five slots under Samples in the right-click menu
Note — a loaded loop is treated as eight beats long whatever its actual length, so a loop of another length plays at the wrong speed
Menu — Samples — the five numbered items under this label each load a WAV file into that slot, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Sample player for a folder of WAV files, playing every channel of a multi-channel file at once through a polyphonic output
Restarts the chosen file from its start position
A rising edge restarts the chosen file from its start position; with nothing patched here the file plays without waiting
Attenuates the pitch CV, from nothing through to its full range
Shifts the playback speed by a volt per octave after the attenuator, read per channel from a polyphonic cable
Attenuates the volume CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets the level, 10V for full level falling to silence at 0V, read per channel from a polyphonic cable
Steps forward one file in the folder; with a cable in the SAMPLE CV input this has no effect
A rising edge steps forward one file in the folder
Steps back one file in the folder; with a cable in the SAMPLE CV input this has no effect
A rising edge steps back one file in the folder
When on, playback returns to the start position as it passes the end position
Above 1V playback returns to the start position as it passes the end position
Picks which file in the folder plays, from the first to the last
Attenuates the SAMPLE selection CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the file selection after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the whole folder
Sets where playback begins, from the start of the file to its end
Attenuates the START CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the start position after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the whole file
Sets where playback ends, from the start of the file to its end; a start later than the end swaps the two
Attenuates the END CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the end position after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the whole file
Sets how long the fade in at the start of the played region lasts, from none to half the region
Attenuates the ATTACK CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the attack time after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Sets how long the fade down lasts, from none to half the region; turned fully clockwise the level is held instead
Attenuates the DECAY CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the decay time after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Splits the played region into 1 to 16 parts, and EOC fires at the end of each one
The first channel of the file being played, -5V to 5V
The second channel of the file being played; a single-channel file is carried on both of these outputs
Every channel of the file on its own polyphonic channel, -5V to 5V
A 1ms 10V trigger at the end of the played region, and at each division point set by DIVISION
Note — the outputs stay silent until a folder is chosen with Select Directory Containing WAV Files in the right-click menu; the module holds no files of its own
Menu — Select Directory Containing WAV Files — points the module at a folder of files to play
Menu — Sample Change Behavior — Restart begins a newly chosen file at the start position, Continual carries on from the position already reached
Menu — Envelope Mode — AD Envelope (decay after attack), Start/End (attack at start, decay at end), or Disabled
Menu — Smoothing — fades across a jump in playback rather than cutting it, which removes the click
wavbankmc.notes: The Trigger Mode submenu is commented out in the 2.41.1 widget, so it is not in the menu and is not described.

lines: Breakbeat player with six sixteen-step sequencers driving position, sample choice, volume, pan, reverse and ratcheting, and sixteen memory slots holding those sequences
Selects that memory slot, loading its six sequences; with COPY armed, pressing a slot copies the sequences of the current slot into it
Arms copying, so the next memory slot pressed receives a copy of the sequences in the current slot; pressing it again disarms
Erases all six sequences in the current memory slot
The clock the loop follows, taken at sixteenth notes; the tempo is worked out from the time between two rising edges, and no sound is made until two have arrived
A rising edge returns the sequencers and the playback position to the start and holds everything until the next clock
A rising edge jumps to the slice chosen by the position sequence without waiting for the next clock
Picks which of the sixteen memory slots is loaded, 0-10V across the sixteen; with a cable here the memory buttons are ignored
Replaces the position sequence, 0-10V choosing one of the sixteen slices of the loop, and below about 0.6V playback runs on undisturbed
Replaces the sample sequence, 0-10V spanning the eight loaded loops
Replaces the volume sequence, 0-10V for silence to full level
Replaces the pan sequence, 0V hard left through 5V centre to 10V hard right
Replaces the reverse sequence; above 5V playback runs backwards through the loop
Replaces the ratchet sequence, 0V for no ratcheting and higher voltages picking one of five faster repeat rates
The value the position sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The value the sample sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The value the volume sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The value the pan sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The value the reverse sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The value the ratchet sequence holds at the current step, 0-10V
The left channel of the loop being played, after volume and pan
The right channel of the loop being played, after volume and pan
The left channel of that loop, carrying sound only while the sample sequence has chosen it
The right channel of that loop, carrying sound only while the sample sequence has chosen it
Note — the tabs across the display choose which of the six sequences is drawn and edited: Position, Sample, Volume, Pan, Reverse and Ratchet
Note — the outputs stay silent until a loop is loaded into one of the eight slots under Samples in the right-click menu, and until two clock pulses have arrived at CLOCK
Menu — Samples — the eight numbered items under this label each load a WAV file into that slot, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Load first 8 WAV files from a folder — opens a folder browser and puts that folder's first eight WAV files into the eight slots in name order
Granular sample player: short looping grains are spawned from one position in a loaded sample and pile up into a cloud
Sets how long each grain is, from a five hundredth of a second to half a second
Attenuates the LENGTH CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the grain length after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Sets how many grains may sound at once, up to 120, with the oldest removed as the count is passed
Attenuates the QUOTA CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the grain count after its attenuator, 0-10V covering none to 120
Sets how many grains are spawned each second, from 10 to 500
Attenuates the SPAWN CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the spawn rate after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Sets where in the sample new grains begin, from its start to its end
Attenuates the playback position CV, from nothing through to its full range
Adds to the playback position after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the whole sample
Shifts the playback speed of every grain by a volt per octave, from -2V to 2V
Adds to the playback speed, a volt per octave
Silences every grain sounding at that moment, leaving new ones to spawn
A rising edge silences every grain sounding at that moment
Scatters the start position of each new grain over a range of about a thousand samples either way
Above 0V the start position of each new grain is scattered, and the switch is then ignored
Sets the output level, from silence through unity at the centre to twice the level
The left channel of the grain cloud
The right channel of the grain cloud
Note — the outputs stay silent until a WAV file is loaded: right-click the panel and click the item under the Sample label, which reads [ EMPTY ] until then
Menu — Sample — the item under this label loads the WAV file the grains are cut from, and prints the filename it holds
Menu — Remove Sample — empties the sample slot and silences every grain sounding at that moment
ghosts.notes: Param 13 (MODES) and param 9 (a pitch attenuator) exist in the code but have no control on the panel and no menu item; the module always runs in mode 0, whose figures are the ones quoted here.

lines: Audio mangler: incoming sound is written to a short buffer and read back through one of fourteen glitching effects, among them bit-crushing bytebeat equations, delays, slice repeats and wave folding
Picks which of the fourteen effects the buffer is read through; with a cable in the EFFECT input this attenuates that voltage instead, 10V covering all fourteen
Sets how much of the buffer the effect works over, from 10 samples to a full second; with a cable in the BUFFER SIZE input this attenuates that voltage instead
Sets how much of the buffer output is written back into the buffer, none to all of it; with a cable in the FEEDBACK input this attenuates that voltage instead
Sets the first parameter of the chosen effect, 0 to 1, and what it changes depends on which effect is chosen; with a cable in the PARAM1 input this attenuates that voltage instead
Sets the second parameter of the chosen effect, 0 to 1, and what it changes depends on which effect is chosen; with a cable in the PARAM2 input this attenuates that voltage instead
Picks the effect, 0-10V across the fourteen, attenuated by the EFFECT knob
Sets the buffer length, 0-10V from 10 samples to a full second, attenuated by the BUFFER SIZE knob
Sets the feedback, 0-10V from none to all of it, attenuated by the FEEDBACK knob
Sets the first parameter of the chosen effect, 0-10V, attenuated by the PARAM1 knob
Sets the second parameter of the chosen effect, 0-10V, attenuated by the PARAM2 knob
The left channel of the audio to mangle
The right channel of the audio to mangle
The left channel of the mangled audio
The right channel of the mangled audio
Note — the name of the chosen effect is shown on the panel readout
Note — the outputs are silent until audio is patched into the inputs; the module makes no sound of its own
satanonaut.notes: Params 0 (clock division), 6 (purge) and 7 (drive) exist in the code but have no control on the panel; drive stays at its default of 1, so the output is not scaled.

lines: Blank panel carrying the Satanonaut artwork, with no controls and no jacks
Note — the module has no controls, no jacks and no processing of any kind; it puts the Satanonaut artwork in the rack and nothing else
Eight stereo sample players in one module, each with its own trigger, start position, level, pan, on switch and pair of outputs, plus a stereo mix
Sets the level of that sample player, from silence to the full level of the file
Places that sample player in the stereo field, hard left through centre to hard right
Sets where in the file that player starts when triggered, 0-10V from the beginning to the end; it is read at the moment the trigger arrives
A rising edge plays that file from the start position; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
When off, that player is silenced at its own outputs and taken out of the mix
The left channel of that sample player, after its level and pan
The right channel of that sample player, after its level and pan
The left channels of all eight players added together
The right channels of all eight players added together
Note — a player stays silent until a WAV file is loaded into it from the right-click menu, either one at a time or eight at once from a folder
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Load individual samples — the eight numbered items under this label each open a file browser for that player, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Load first 8 WAV files from a folder — opens a folder browser and puts that folder's first eight WAV files into the eight players in name order
Word player holding ten banks of spoken words, with the bank and the word chosen by knob or CV and a word spoken on each trigger
Picks the bank, through the ten: pronouns, verbs, descriptors, nouns, connectors, time, emotions, numbers, questions and a custom bank of your own files
Attenuates the BANK CV, from nothing through to its full range
Picks the word within the chosen bank, from its first to its last
Attenuates the WORD CV, from nothing through to its full range
A rising edge speaks the word chosen at that moment; nothing is spoken until a trigger arrives
Shifts the pitch of the spoken word, -5V to 5V for half an octave either way, read at the moment the trigger arrives
Adds to the bank choice after its attenuator, a volt per bank across the ten
Adds to the word choice after its attenuator, 0-10V across the words in the chosen bank
The left channel of the spoken word
The right channel of the spoken word
Note — the ten banks of words are shipped with the plugin, so a word is spoken as soon as a trigger arrives
Menu — Pitch CV Range — Bipolar: -5V to +5V, or Unipolar: 0V to 10V, setting how the PITCH input is read
Menu — Select Directory Containing Word Files — replaces the vocabulary with the WAV and MP3 files in a folder of your own
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Visit r1n.ai — opens that web page in a browser
maya.notes: The PITCH input covers half an octave either way rather than a volt per octave, so it is coloured cv rather than pitch. The bank of your own files is reached with Select Directory Containing Word Files, which replaces the whole vocabulary rather than adding an eleventh bank.

lines: Panel drawn as the Tempest VS-1 hardware controller: its knobs, buttons and switch each have a jack, and incoming MIDI control changes move them
Sets the voltage at the M1 output, 0-10V; an incoming MIDI control change moves it as well
Sets the voltage at the M2 output, 0-10V; an incoming MIDI control change moves it as well
Sets the voltage at the M3 output, 0-10V; an incoming MIDI control change moves it as well
Sets the voltage at the M4 output, 0-10V; an incoming MIDI control change moves it as well
Sets the voltage at that SM output, 0-10V, and an incoming control change moves it as well
Sets the voltage at the Epic output, 0-10V
Sets the voltage at the Center output, 0-10V; an incoming MIDI control change moves it as well
Turning it right fires a trigger at the right encoder output and turning it left fires one at the left encoder output
Fires a 100ms trigger at the Mode output
Fires a 100ms trigger at the Preset output
Fires a 100ms trigger at the Clear output
Sets the A/B switch output to 0V at A and 10V at B; MIDI control change 25 moves it as well
Opens the MIDI driver and device menu for the port that drives this panel
The voltage the M1 knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage the M2 knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage the M3 knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage the M4 knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage that SM knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage the Epic knob is set to, 0-10V
The voltage the Center knob is set to, 0-10V
A 10ms 10V trigger each time the encoder is turned one step to the left
A 10ms 10V trigger each time the encoder is turned one step to the right
A 100ms 10V trigger when the Mode button is pressed, or when control change 23 arrives
A 100ms 10V trigger when the Preset button is pressed, or when control change 22 arrives
A 100ms 10V trigger when the Clear button is pressed, or when control change 24 arrives
0V while the switch is at A and 10V while it is at B
Note — no MIDI reaches the panel until a device is chosen: the MIDI button opens a menu of drivers and devices, and the panel's own right-click menu holds nothing
Menu — MIDI Driver — on the menu the MIDI button opens, not the panel menu: picks which of Rack's MIDI drivers the port uses
Menu — MIDI Device — on the menu the MIDI button opens, not the panel menu: picks the device to receive from, or (No device)
tempest-vs1.notes: The MIDI mapping in the 2.41.1 code is written for a Launch Control XL MK2 for testing: control changes 13 to 19 move SM4, SM2, M4, SM3, SM1, M3 and Center in that order, and 29 and 30 move M1 and M2. The Epic knob has no control change of its own, and the comments in the code name different knobs from the ones the mapping table actually reaches. The panel's own right-click menu is empty; the MIDI driver and device lists are opened by left-clicking the MIDI button.

lines: Eight-track sample player driven over OSC: another program loads the files and sets volume, pitch and triggers, and the tracks are time-stretched to a master clock
A rising edge starts the master clock
A rising edge stops the master clock
A rising edge returns the master clock to its start and cues every loaded track to the next sync point
The eight tracks added together, left channel
The eight tracks added together, right channel
The left channel of each track on its own polyphonic channel, eight channels
The right channel of each track on its own polyphonic channel, eight channels
A 10ms 10V trigger at each sync point of the master clock
Note — the module holds no files of its own and makes no sound until another program sends it OSC messages loading samples into its tracks
Note — the tempo of a loaded file is taken from its filename, which is why the example in the menu ends in 120bpm
Note — the right-click menu lists the OSC commands the module accepts: load, volume, pitch and trigger per track, and bpm, start, stop and restart
Menu — OSC Port — the UDP port OSC messages are received on, 7000 until it is changed, with the current port printed beside the item
Menu — Reset Counters — returns the counts of messages received and dropped to zero
kaiseki.notes: Outputs 0 to 15, the per-track left and right jacks, are declared and written in the code but have no jack on the panel, so they carry no line and no family.

lines: Sixteen sliders held in twenty-four banks, each slider sent to its own output and to a polyphonic output
Selects that bank, so the sliders show and put out the values stored in it; with COPY, CLEAR or RNDM armed, pressing a bank copies into it, empties it or fills it with random values
Arms copying, so the next bank pressed receives a copy of the bank showing; pressing it again returns to plain bank selection
Arms clearing, so the next bank pressed is emptied; pressing it again returns to plain bank selection
Arms randomising, so the next bank pressed is filled with random slider values; pressing it again returns to plain bank selection
Steps back one bank, wrapping round to the last one
Steps forward one bank, wrapping round to the first one
Picks the bank directly, 0-10V across the twenty-four, and while a cable is patched here the bank buttons are overridden
A rising edge steps forward one bank
A rising edge steps back one bank
A rising edge returns to the first bank
A polyphonic input added to the sliders, channel by channel, before they reach the outputs
The value of that slider in the bank showing, in the voltage range chosen for it, plus anything on that channel of the poly add input
All sixteen slider values on one polyphonic cable, in the same order as the individual outputs
Note — drag a slider to set its value; a slider carries no label until one is typed into the Labels submenu of the right-click menu
Menu — Slider #1 through Slider #16 — each holds an Output Range submenu setting the span that slider covers, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with
Menu — Match Cable Colors — draws each slider in the colour of the cable patched to its output
Menu — Visualize Summed Voltages — draws what the polyphonic add input adds to each slider
Menu — Labels — opens sixteen text fields, one per slider, for a name of your own
digitalprogrammer.notes: The source builds a per-slider Snap submenu, but the struct that holds it is never added to any menu and snap_settings is never read in processing, so Snap cannot be reached and is not described.

lines: Six sequencers in one module, each drawing a voltage sequence and a gate sequence of up to 32 steps, with its own length, clock and pair of outputs
Selects that sequencer for editing, so the display draws its voltage and gate steps
Sets how many steps that sequencer plays before returning to its first, 1 to 32
A rising edge advances every sequencer that has no cable in its own step input
A rising edge returns every sequencer to its first step, and clock pulses are ignored for the following 1ms
A rising edge advances that sequencer alone, in place of the common STEP input
The voltage drawn at the current step of that sequencer, in the range chosen for it
A 10ms 10V trigger on every step marked in the gate sequence of that sequencer
Note — drag in the upper half of the display to draw voltages and in the lower half to set gates
Note — Quick Key Reference in the right-click menu lists the keys the display responds to, among them f to freeze the sequencers for editing and r to randomise the sequence under the pointer
Note — every step of every sequence starts at zero, so the voltage outputs stay at the bottom of their range and no gate is put out until the display is drawn on
Menu — Sequencer Settings — All Sequencers, and Sequencer #1 through Sequencer #6, each holding that sequencer's Output Range, Snap and Sample & Hold
Menu — Snap — None, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 32 or 36, rounding drawn voltages to that many steps; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Sample & Hold — Off or On, holding the voltage output between gates instead of changing it every step; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Reset Mode — two choices printed Next clock input. and Instant, setting whether a reset takes effect on the next clock or at once
Menu — Output Range — the span of a sequencer's voltage output, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Quick Key Reference — lists the keys the display responds to while the pointer is over the module
digitalsequencer.notes: Input 0 (CLOCK), outputs 0 and 1 (CLOCK and END) and params 0, 7 and 14 are declared in the code but have no jack or control on the panel; the freeze toggle is reached by the f key rather than by a button.

lines: Sixteen sequencers in one module, each drawing a voltage sequence and a gate sequence of up to 32 steps, with all sixteen reaching the outside on polyphonic cables
Selects that sequencer for editing, so the display draws its voltage and gate steps
Advances the sequencers: a polyphonic cable steps each sequencer from its own channel, and a single channel steps all sixteen together
Sets the lengths, channel by channel, 0-10V for 1 to 32 steps; a sequencer with no channel of its own keeps the length it was given
A rising edge returns every sequencer to its first step, and clock pulses are ignored for the following 1ms
The voltage drawn at the current step of each sequencer, one channel per sequencer, in the range chosen for it
A 10ms 10V trigger on every step marked in the gate sequence, one channel per sequencer
Note — drag in the upper half of the display to draw voltages and in the lower half to set gates
Note — Quick Key Reference in the right-click menu lists the keys the display responds to: f to freeze for editing, g to send a gate while frozen, and r to randomise the sequence under the pointer
Note — every step of every sequence starts at zero, so the voltage output stays at the bottom of its range and no gate is put out until the display is drawn on
Note — holding shift and dragging on the display shifts the sequence under the pointer left or right
Menu — Sequencer Settings — All Sequencers, and Sequencer #1 through Sequencer #16, each holding that sequencer's Output Range, Snap and Sample & Hold
Menu — Snap — None, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 32 or 36, rounding drawn voltages to that many steps; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Sample & Hold — Off or On, holding the voltage output between gates instead of changing it every step; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Reset Mode — two choices printed Next clock input. and Instant, setting whether a reset takes effect on the next clock or at once
Menu — Output Range — the span of a sequencer's voltage output, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with; reached through Sequencer Settings
Menu — Quick Key Reference — lists the keys the display responds to while the pointer is over the module
digitalsequencerxp.notes: Input 3 (POLY_MOD_INPUT) and param 16 (the freeze toggle) are in the code but not on the panel; the input's jack is commented out in the widget, and freezing is reached by the f key.

lines: Sample player with 32 cue markers: markers are placed on the waveform and each fires its own trigger output as playback passes it
Selects that marker number, so a marker placed on the waveform belongs to it and fires its output; one at a time is lit
Starts playback from the position the playhead has reached
Stops playback, leaving the playhead where it is
Returns the playhead to the start of the sample
A rising edge starts playback
A rising edge stops playback
A rising edge returns the playhead to the start of the sample
The left channel of the sample, -5V to 5V
The right channel of the sample, -5V to 5V
A 10V trigger as the playhead passes a marker belonging to that number, 1ms long unless the menu says otherwise
Note — the outputs stay silent until a WAV file is loaded, with the item under the Sample label in the right-click menu
Note — double-click the large waveform to add a marker for the selected number, and double-click a marker to delete it
Note — drag the large waveform sideways to move the view along the sample, drag a marker to move it, and drag the playhead to move the playback position
Note — the scroll wheel over the large waveform zooms the view in and out around the pointer
Note — right-click the large waveform for Clear All Markers and Add Marker; right-click a marker for Delete Marker
Menu — Sample — the item under this label loads the WAV file, and prints the filename it holds
Menu — Trigger Length — how long every marker pulse lasts, from 1ms to 200ms
Menu — Place markers at divisions — spreads markers evenly through the sample, at 4, 8, 16 or 32 of them
Menu — Loop sample playback — returns to the start at the end of the sample instead of stopping
Menu — Lock Markers — stops markers being added, moved or deleted
Menu — Enable Vertical-Drag Zoom — makes a drag up or down on the large waveform zoom the view as the drag sideways moves it
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out
Menu — Clear All Markers — removes every marker
Menu — Lock Mouse Interaction — stops the waveform responding to the mouse at all
Menu — Clear markers on sample load — empties the markers whenever a new file is loaded
cue_research.notes: The large waveform carries two right-click menus of its own, one over empty waveform and one over a marker; both are described in Note lines.

lines: Arpeggiator and step sequencer in one: held polyphonic notes are arpeggiated on an incoming clock, while four drawn sequences add gate length, transposition and two modulation outputs
When on, the held notes keep playing after the gates are released, until new notes arrive
When on, the arpeggio runs whether or not gates are held
Sets the clock division of the arpeggio, from a division by eight through unity to a multiplication by eight
Attenuates and inverts the RATE CV, -1 to 1
Picks the order the held notes are played in: as played, forwards, backwards, pendulum or random, and the second five repeat each note twice
Attenuates and inverts the SHAPE CV, -1 to 1
Sets how many times round the sequence before that step's value is applied, 1 to 16
The notes to arpeggiate, one per polyphonic channel, read as a volt per octave
The gates that say which notes are held, one per polyphonic channel
The clock the arpeggio runs on; the gate length is worked out from the time between two rising edges
A rising edge returns the arpeggio and all four sequences to their first step
Adds to the clock division after its attenuverter, the range chosen on the menu
Adds to the note order after its attenuverter, the range chosen on the menu
The note being played, as a volt per octave, with the transposition sequence added and quantized if the menu says so
A 10V gate whose length is set by the gate sequence, from nothing to the full step
The first modulation sequence, in the range and polarity set for it, with the slew set for it
The second modulation sequence, in the range and polarity set for it, with the slew set for it
A 10V trigger whenever a step passes its chance roll, on the sequence chosen in the menu
A 10V trigger whenever a cycle counter reaches zero, on the sequence chosen in the menu
Note — the display holds four pages, Gate, Transpose, Mod 1 and Mod 2, each with a row of drawn values, a percentage row setting the chance that the step is applied, and the row of cycle selectors
Note — nothing is played until polyphonic notes and gates are patched in and a clock is patched into CLOCK
Note — a drawn value row carries its own right-click menu, with Shift Left, Shift Right, Randomize, Reverse, Shuffle, Invert, Sort, Mirror, Reset to Default, Zero, Undo and Redo
Note — drag across a value row to draw it, double-click a step to return it to its default, and hold shift while dragging to move the whole row sideways
Menu — Probability Output Settings — holds Source, choosing which of the four sequences the PROB output follows, and Trigger Length
Menu — Cycle Output Settings — holds Source, choosing which of the four sequences the CYCLE output follows, and Trigger Length
Menu — Quantize Output Settings — holds Enable, turning quantizing of the pitch output on, and Scale and Root Note
Menu — Rate Attenuverter Response — -5V to +5V or -10V to +10V, setting the span the RATE CV is read over
Menu — Reset Cycles — on a cycle selector's own right-click menu, not the panel menu: returns every cycle counter to the start
Menu — Legacy Reset Mode — accepts clock pulses immediately after a reset instead of ignoring them briefly
Menu — Shape Attenuverter Response — -5V to +5V or -10V to +10V, setting the span the SHAPE CV is read over
Menu — Smart Randomize — on a cycle selector's own right-click menu, not the panel menu: fills the cycle selectors with values that fit the sequence
arpseq.notes: Reset Cycles and Smart Randomize are on the cycle selector knob's own menu, not the panel menu, and the drawn value rows carry a menu of their own.

lines: Eight-track sample-based drum machine: sixteen steps per track, a knob per step for any of sixteen parameters, and sixteen memory slots holding whole patterns
Turns that step of the selected track on or off
Sets the value of the chosen parameter at that step of the selected track, which is what a parameter lock is
Makes the step knobs set the level of the selected track, step by step
Makes the step knobs set the stereo position of the selected track, step by step
Makes the step knobs set the playback speed of the selected track, step by step
Makes the step knobs set how many times the sample repeats within that step of the selected track
Makes the step knobs set where in the sample playback begins at that step of the selected track
Makes the step knobs set where in the sample playback ends at that step of the selected track
Makes the step knobs set the chance that the step plays at all, from never to every time
Makes the step knobs set whether the sample repeats between its start and end points at that step
Makes the step knobs set whether the sample plays backwards at that step
Makes the step knobs set the fade in at the start of the sample at that step
Makes the step knobs set the fade away at the end of the sample at that step, up to 4 seconds
Makes the step knobs set how much of the track's delay is heard at that step
Makes the step knobs set the delay time of the selected track at that step
Makes the step knobs set how much of the delay is fed back into itself at that step
Makes the step knobs set the filter frequency of the selected track at that step
Makes the step knobs set the filter resonance of the selected track at that step
Selects that memory slot, loading the sequences and parameter locks stored in it for all eight tracks
Marks the memory slot showing as the one to copy from
Writes the copied memory slot over the one showing
Sets the level of the stereo mix, from silence to eight times the summed tracks
Advances the sequence one step every eight rising edges, with the pulses in between used for ratcheting
A rising edge returns every track to its first step
Picks the memory slot, 0-10V across the sixteen
The left channel of all eight tracks mixed, after the master level
The right channel of all eight tracks mixed, after the master level
The left channel of that track alone, before the master level
The right channel of that track alone, before the master level
Note — no track makes a sound until a sample is loaded into it, either from the right-click menu or by double-clicking that track's window in the display
Note — clicking a track window in the display chooses which track the step buttons and step knobs edit
Note — a track window carries its own right-click menu, headed Track Menu, with Load Sample, Clear Track Steps, Reset Track Parameters, Clear and Reset Both, and Unassign Sample
Note — a step knob carries its own right-click menu, with Randomize Knobs, Reset Knobs, Increase all knobs by 1 notch and Decrese all knobs by 1 notch
Note — a step button carries its own right-click menu, with Clear All Parameter Locks for this Step, Copy Step, Paste Step, Shift Steps Right, Shift Steps Left, Randomize Steps and Clear Steps
Note — double-clicking a step knob returns it to its default value, and holding shift while double-clicking returns every step knob of that parameter to it
Note — the module counts eight clock pulses per step, so a sequence advances at an eighth of the rate arriving at the clock input
Note — the step knob menu also holds Set all knobs' values to this knob's value, and two items shifting all sixteen knob values one step left or right
Menu — Load individual samples — the eight numbered items under this label each load a WAV file into that track, and each prints the filename it holds
Menu — Tracks — Track #1 through Track #8, each holding Sample Position Snap Division, Clear Track Data and Unassign Sample
Menu — All Tracks — holds Shift All Sequences, which moves every track's sequence one step left or right
Menu — LCD Color Theme — Cool White, Soft Yellow, Legacy Red, Ice Blue or Data Green, setting the colour the display is drawn in
Menu — Initialize — clears everything the module holds, after a confirmation item inside the submenu
Menu — Load first 8 WAV files from a folder — opens a folder browser and puts that folder's first eight WAV files into the eight tracks in name order
Menu — Export Kit — packs the eight loaded sample files into one archive, with a list naming the track each belongs to
Menu — Import Kit — unpacks an archive written by Export Kit into a folder you choose and loads its eight samples into the tracks
Menu — Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out; under the Audio Quality label
groovebox.notes: Params 16 to 31 (step select buttons) and 64 to 71 are declared in the code but have no control on the panel. Three of the module's menus are not on the panel: the track windows, the step knobs and the step buttons each carry their own right-click menu, and those are described in Note lines.

lines: Mixer and gate expander for Groove Box, placed immediately to the left of it, adding mute, solo, level, pan and pitch per track and a trigger output per track
Silences that track of Groove Box
Leaves only the soloed tracks of Groove Box sounding
Sets the level of that track, from silence through unity at the centre to twice the level
Places that track in the stereo field, hard left through centre to hard right
Shifts the playback speed of that track, -1 to 1
Any voltage other than 0V mutes that track, alongside its mute button
A 10ms 10V trigger each time that track of Groove Box plays a step
Note — nothing is sent or received unless Groove Box is the module immediately to the right
Menu — Exclusive Solo — on a SOLO button's own right-click menu, not the panel menu: solos that track and clears the solo on every other
Menu — Unsolo All — on a SOLO button's own right-click menu, not the panel menu: clears the solo on every track
Menu — Unmute All — on a MUTE button's own right-click menu, not the panel menu: clears the mute on every track
GrooveBoxExpander.notes: Exclusive Solo and Unsolo All are on a SOLO button's own menu and Unmute All on a MUTE button's; the panel menu holds none of them.
